name: DePix App
description: Non-custodial Pix payment gateway on the Liquid Network. Agents can accept Pix payments (checkouts/products), on-ramp BRL to DePix and off-ramp DePix to Pix via REST API. DePix is the BRL stablecoin; DePix App is the gateway service.

urls.api_base_note: Every documented path already carries its own /api/ prefix, e.g. https://api.depixapp.com/api/checkouts. Do not append /api to this base.

scope_families.merchant_*: Merchant/gateway side — read checkouts, products and account (merchant_read); create charges and CRUD products (merchant_write).
scope_families.wallet_*: Wallet side — read deposit/withdrawal status (wallet_read); move money via on/off-ramp Pix (wallet_write). Never granted by default.

auth.how_to_obtain: Two paths. Human merchants: create an account at https://depixapp.com/app/, open a merchant profile, then create keys in the API Keys area (sandbox keys are immediate). Agent accounts: self-onboard with no email and no dashboard — generate an Ed25519 keypair and call POST /api/agents/register signing the request with it, passing an operator op_… token (a human obtains it once by connecting a GitHub/Google identity in the dashboard); a sandbox key and a wallet-only starter live key are auto-issued in the registration response. See agent_onboarding below and https://depixapp.com/docs/en/#agents.

constraints.custody: non-custodial — the API never holds funds or private keys; signing is client-side
constraints.payer_tax_number: CPF/CNPJ of the PAYER is required on money-moving endpoints (deposit and checkout); a missing value returns 400 tax_number_required.
constraints.rate_limits: per-IP, per-user, per-merchant and optional per-key; 429 with Retry-After
constraints.webhooks: HMAC-signed; checkout.* for all merchants, deposit.*/withdraw.* for API-key operations; status can also be polled
constraints.fees: Deducted from the amount — the DePix credited and the Pix paid out are NET. Deposit 2% + R$ 0,99; withdrawal 1% + R$ 1,00 up to R$ 100,00 and 2% above it. Current rates and worked examples: https://depixapp.com/en/#landing-fees

agent_sdk.name: @depixapp/sdk
agent_sdk.role: engine lineage / code-level SDK — NOT the primary agent surface
agent_sdk.summary: The code-level lineage of the same wallet engine that powers the 27 `wallet_*` tools inside `@depixapp/mcp`. Non-custodial Liquid-Network wallet SDK for autonomous agents: wallet-first, intent-based API — create/restore a wallet from a seed the agent controls, then convert(), quote(), send(), receive(), deposit() and withdraw() across assets and networks, with routing, settlement and crash-recovery built in. Reach for it when YOU are writing the code; when an AGENT is driving, connect `@depixapp/mcp` instead (see the `mcp` block) — that is the successor public surface.
agent_sdk.custody: non-custodial — the seed never leaves the agent; all signing is client-side
agent_sdk.mcp_server: Do NOT run this package as an MCP server. The wallet tools (wallet_convert, wallet_quote, wallet_send, …) ship inside `@depixapp/mcp` — run `npx -y @depixapp/mcp` (stdio, 49 tools, first run `npx -y @depixapp/mcp init`). See the `mcp` block.
agent_sdk.relationship: Same engine, two surfaces. `@depixapp/mcp` (Apache-2.0) is the agent-facing surface and the one to reach for; this SDK is the code-level lineage of its wallet engine and stays published for code-first integrations. This REST API is the Pix on/off-ramp and merchant side that both consume.
agent_sdk.lightning: lightning_pay / lightning_receive settle through Boltz swaps; DePix itself is not issued on Lightning.

mcp.summary: ONE MCP server with TWO levels of access — not two products. `@depixapp/mcp` registers 49 tools. Connected to the DePix App-hosted endpoint it exposes the keyless 22 (receive side). Run by the operator over stdio with a seed, the same package exposes all 49, the extra 27 being the `wallet_*` tools that hold, sign and move funds. The split is custody, not features withheld: signing happens in-process, so whichever process runs a wallet tool IS the seed holder, and DePix App holds no seeds.
levels: 2 — local (npx -y @depixapp/mcp, operator's seed, 49 tools, full wallet)

gateway.auth: OAuth 2.1 connector (claude.ai / ChatGPT — capped to read + merchant scopes) or `Authorization: Bearer sk_test_…|sk_live_…`. The key is forwarded verbatim per request and never stored.
gateway.summary: Twenty-two tools over this REST API. Sixteen are merchant side — this server reads and creates checkouts and products but never creates deposits or withdrawals, so it cannot move funds on its own. The other six are support-ticket tools (open, get, list, reply, close a support ticket, and attach a file to one). This deployment holds no seed, so the 27 `wallet_*` tools are structurally absent from it.

environment_variables.DEPIX_API_KEY: required for the 22 gateway tools — sk_test_ / sk_live_.
environment_variables.DEPIX_WALLET_PASSPHRASE: required for the 27 wallet tools — unlocks the seed created by `init`. Absent, the wallet tools stay listed and return a typed `wallet_not_configured` error naming `npx -y @depixapp/mcp init`.
environment_variables.DEPIX_WALLET_DIR: optional — where the encrypted wallet lives; defaults to the per-user data directory.

wallet.first_run: `npx -y @depixapp/mcp init` — a TTY-only human ceremony that creates or restores the wallet and prints the paste-ready `mcpServers` block. Seed creation is deliberately NOT an MCP tool: the mnemonic must never transit model context or conversation logs.
wallet.transport_safety: stdio is the only default-safe transport for this level. The server loads the seed process-wide and carries no auth of its own; exposing it over HTTP without operator-provided auth + network isolation lets anyone who reaches the port drain the wallet.
wallet.summary: The same server, run where the agent lives, holding the operator's seed. Adds 27 `wallet_*` tools (balances, addresses, Pix on/off-ramp, send, convert, Lightning, gift cards, guardrails, recovery) for 49 total; these tools MOVE FUNDS, signed in-process on the operator's machine. Non-custodial: the seed never leaves it.

agent_onboarding.summary: Agents can self-onboard via /api/agents/* instead of a human creating keys in the dashboard.
agent_onboarding.auth: Per-request Ed25519 signature over the agent's own keypair, plus an operator token (op_…) a human obtains once by connecting an identity in the dashboard.
agent_onboarding.status_endpoint: GET /api/agents/status — account status, graduation progress and the read-only `pacing` limits, so the agent can pace itself instead of discovering caps through 4xx.
